subject.title: Follow-up: optimize fallback order + add model-input config guardrail

question: What canonical fallback-order policy and configured model-input capability contract should OpenClaw enforce for `models.providers.*.models[*].input`?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but choosing cost-first versus latency/quality ordering and choosing whether to reject, warn, or override-gate disputed modalities can change existing user config and provider routing behavior.

options.title: Policy Artifact Plus Capability Guardrail
options.body: Keep explicit operator fallback order as the default, publish benchmark guidance for recommended chains, and add capability-aware validation or warnings with an intentional override path for custom providers.

options.title: Strict Schema Rejection
options.body: Reject unsupported or disputed modalities at config validation time, accepting a compatibility break only with a doctor migration and clear release note.

options.title: Defer To Focused Trackers
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50287 own only model-input guardrails and open a separate fallback-policy item if maintainers do not want this umbrella tracker.

recommendation.title: Policy Artifact Plus Capability Guardrail
recommendation.body: Keep explicit operator fallback order as the default, publish benchmark guidance for recommended chains, and add capability-aware validation or warnings with an intentional override path for custom providers.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across model fallback policy, media-understanding defaults, provider docs, and product-scope review.
